driftFormulaAndChargeSign.derivation: In time Delta t, carriers with mean directed speed magnitude v cross a uniform section S from a swept volume S*v*Delta t. For one carrier species of density n and charge q0, the transferred charge magnitude is |Delta Q| = |q0|*n*S*v*Delta t. Thus |I| = |Delta Q|/Delta t = |q0|*n*S*v, giving v = |I|/(|q0|*n*S). For electrons q0 = -e; their mean directed velocity is opposite conventional current, whereas the reported speed magnitude is positive. This is directed drift, not the much faster random microscopic electron motion. The modern text states both absolute-value and directed-motion distinctions.

waterAnalogy.derivation: In a filled pipe, a pressure disturbance travels as a mechanical wave, while fluid transport is the mean material flow. Wave speed depends on compressibility and pipe compliance; bulk flow speed depends on the flow conditions and can be much slower. The source's illustrative several-hundred-m/s disturbance and several-tens-of-cm/s transport values are both retained. They express different physical quantities, not a universal acoustic speed of water. Modern very-quick wording describes arrival after finite propagation, not literal simultaneous motion at every point.
